## The deliverable

Exactly one new `files[]` entry:

1. Read the upstream blob from `objectstack-ai/objectstack` at the ref this port was taken from. ⚠️ **Deriving that ref is the real work of this card** — it is ⛔ not "whatever is on upstream `main` today". A ref chosen for convenience silently converts every later upstream improvement into a declared divergence, which is the opposite of what the gate is for. Say how you determined it and what would have been wrong with the alternatives.
2. Compute its SHA-256 for `upstreamSha256`.
3. Declare every divergence as an exact `upstream` / `ported` text pair with a `why` of ≥ 10 characters. `validatePin` enforces the shape **and** that each declared snippet matches **exactly once** — so a snippet that appears twice fails, and the fix is a longer snippet, ⛔ never a weaker one.

The card names one divergence that already exists: the shebang-census half, where this repo measures **0** shebang-only scripts while upstream treats that half as load-bearing. ⛔ Do not assume it is the only one — diff the two files and declare what is there.

## ⭐ The acceptance probe, which triage wrote and I am keeping

The gate's own green line today reads `3 ported file(s) match … each at its own pinned ref (2 distinct: …)`. After this it must read **4**. ⚠️ The "distinct refs" count may go to **3** or stay at **2** depending on the ref you derive — ⛔ report which and why, don't let it pass unremarked either way.

⚠️ **And triage's stop condition, which is the important half:** the diff must touch **exactly one new entry**. If it touches more, **stop and report** — that means something re-synced entries that were not part of this work. ⛔ Do not "fix" the extra churn; it is a finding.

## ⛔ Fences — binding

- ⛔ **No change to the pin schema itself.** Out of scope by triage's ruling.
- ⛔ **objectui#8385 item 1** (the prose fix) is landed separately and is not this card.
- ⛔ Do not modify `scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs` itself, and ⛔ do not "port" upstream improvements into it on this round — registering the file is the deliverable; carrying a construct across is a different card with its own review surface.
- ⛔ Do not touch any existing `files[]` entry, above all the `.claude/hooks/` one.
- ⛔ **Governed surface** (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `docs/adr/**`) is out of scope. ⛔ **Never edit `content/docs/releases/`.**
- ⛔ **Worktree-first**, one dedicated worktree; never edit a shared primary checkout. ⛔ **Never `git stash`** — `refs/stash` lives in the common `.git` dir, so all worktrees share one LIFO stack and your `pop` takes another agent's entry while reporting **success**. Use a patch or a wip commit.
- ⛔ Never skip, disable or weaken a test; never lower a floor or raise a ratchet ceiling; never rebase/amend/force-push a pushed branch.
- ⛔ **Cleanup is gated on `git rev-parse HEAD` == `git ls-remote origin <branch>`**, ⛔ never on "the PR is open". A round in this lane nearly lost its final commit that way.

## Measurement discipline

- ⛔ A grep line count is not an entity count — exclude comment lines (`grep -vE '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(\*|//|/\*)'`) and **print the matched lines**.
- Every absence claim needs a **control with a known direction that HITS in the same run**.
- Capture exit codes by **redirect-then-capture**, ⛔ never through a pipe.
- Run `scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs` before and after and quote **both** verdict lines verbatim — the before-line is what makes the after-line readable.
- ⛔ A ruling is not a reading, a report is not a reading, and the table above is a reading of mine that you should redo.
